briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Crosses $17B as National Rescheduling and Psilocybin Cases Build Steam
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just topped $17 billion in lifetime sales and Ann Arbor keeps adding storefronts, even as the fight over the 24% wholesale tax spills into the governor's race. Nationally, the DEA's own rescheduling brief argues cannabis no longer belongs in Schedule I while Compass Pathways pushes its psilocybin therapy toward a 2027 launch — real momentum for operators willing to play the long game.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17 billion in lifetime sales — August alone added roughly $259 million, and the state's cumulative adult-use and medical haul has generated an estimated $2.66 billion in taxes.
Lume opens new Ann Arbor storefront — the Michigan-based chain debuted its 2247 W. Liberty Street location with a three-day grand opening running 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.
GOP governor candidate vows to repeal the wholesale tax — John James has pledged to kill or slash the 24% levy after industry executives backed his campaign with roughly $90,000 in contributions.

Market stabilizes after January's tax shock — sales climbed back to $255.4 million by March and held near $253.5 million through June, with cultivators absorbing most of the wholesale tax hit rather than consumers.

State drops record fine on a vape manufacturer — regulators hit a popular brand with the biggest penalty in Michigan cannabis history, a signal enforcement is tightening the field for compliant operators.

national.text: DEA's own filing says weed doesn't belong in Schedule I — in its final post-hearing brief the agency argued marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, with a judge's recommendation now pending.

Compass Pathways posts durable six-month psilocybin data — 39% of COMP006 patients hit a clinically meaningful response after two doses, an effect that held for about six months, with a rolling NDA submission underway.
FDA fast-tracks COMP360 toward 2027 launch — Compass says it holds breakthrough therapy designation and expects a National Priority Voucher, with a draft label already under agency review.

Vireo Growth scales up with Planet 13 buy — the all-stock merger will leave Vireo operating roughly 265 retail stores and dispensaries across 15 states, cementing it as one of the largest U.S. operators.

States still waiting on rescheduling guidance — California's cannabis regulator says the DEA has shown "any sort of interest" in helping states implement the Trump administration's marijuana move, leaving operators in limbo until a final ruling lands.
